# Method and Apparatus for Managing Communications on a Moving Platform

## Overview

The present disclosure relates to a method and apparatus designed to manage communications for a moving platform. Such a platform incorporates several key components working in coordination: multiple platform applications that generate and consume data, a communications system capable of supporting several wireless communication links, and a data management module that oversees the flow of information across these links. Together, these elements enable efficient and adaptive data transmission in dynamic operating environments where connectivity conditions may vary continuously.

## Monitoring Link Performance

Central to the operation of this system is the continuous monitoring of communication link performance. The data management module receives performance data that indicates the current available bandwidth of each communication link. These links are either allocated to, or otherwise associated with, the various platform applications running on the moving platform. By maintaining an up-to-date picture of available bandwidth across all links, the system establishes the foundation necessary for making informed decisions about data transmission.

## Assessing Application Requirements

For each platform application, the system identifies the bandwidth requirement of the data that is queued or intended for transmission. This bandwidth requirement is then compared against the current available bandwidth of the communication link associated with that particular application. This comparison process is performed on a per-application basis, ensuring that the specific transmission needs of each application are individually evaluated in relation to the resources available to it.

## Generating and Transmitting Information Data

When the comparison reveals that the available bandwidth of a given communication link is insufficient to meet the needs of a specified application, the system responds by generating information data. This information data is then transmitted to the affected application or, alternatively, to a quality of service interface associated with that application. In this way, the relevant component is promptly notified of the bandwidth limitation, allowing corrective action to be taken before transmission is attempted under unsuitable conditions.

## Adapting Application Data for Transmission

Upon receiving the information data, the specified platform application—or its associated quality of service interface—adapts at least one parameter of its application data to align with the current available bandwidth. Through this adaptation, the data is reconfigured so that it can be successfully transmitted to a recipient node despite the constrained link conditions. This adaptive mechanism ensures that communication remains reliable and efficient, even as the available bandwidth of the wireless links fluctuates during operation of the moving platform.

## Summary

In summary, the described method and apparatus provide an intelligent, responsive framework for managing communications on a moving platform. By continuously monitoring link performance, evaluating application-specific bandwidth requirements, and enabling dynamic adaptation of application data, the system maximizes the effective use of available wireless resources and maintains robust connectivity between the platform and recipient nodes.

# Managing Communications on a Moving Platform

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates generally to communication management systems, and more particularly to a method and apparatus for managing communications on a moving platform such as an aircraft, ship, train, or other mobile vehicle where communication link conditions vary continuously with the platform's movement and environment.

## Background

Moving platforms often rely on multiple communication links to support a variety of onboard applications. These applications may include passenger internet services, cockpit or crew communications, telemetry and diagnostic reporting, entertainment systems, and safety-critical data exchanges. Each of these applications carries different data transmission requirements and varying degrees of importance.

A significant challenge arises because the available bandwidth on communication links serving a moving platform is not constant. As the platform travels, factors such as distance from ground stations, satellite positioning, atmospheric interference, and network congestion cause the effective capacity of each link to fluctuate. Without an intelligent management scheme, applications may attempt to transmit data at rates exceeding the current capacity of their assigned links, resulting in dropped packets, degraded performance, and unreliable communications.

## Summary of the Invention

To address these challenges, the present invention provides a method and apparatus for managing communications on a moving platform. The system actively monitors the available bandwidth of multiple communication links, each of which may be allocated to one or more platform applications. For each application, the system compares the application's data transmission requirements against the current capacity of the communication link assigned to it.

When the system determines that a given link's available bandwidth is insufficient to meet the transmission requirements of its associated application, it responds by generating and transmitting information data. This information data prompts the affected application, or its associated quality of service (QoS) interface, to adapt its data transmission parameters accordingly. In this manner, the system enables efficient utilization of available bandwidth and maintains reliable communication even under varying and unpredictable network conditions.

## Detailed Description

### System Architecture

The apparatus includes a bandwidth monitoring module, a comparison and decision module, and an information data generator. The bandwidth monitoring module continuously or periodically measures the available capacity of each communication link supporting the moving platform. These links may include satellite communication channels, cellular connections, line-of-sight radio links, and other wireless communication pathways.

Each communication link is allocated to serve one or more platform applications. The allocation may be static, based on predefined assignments, or dynamic, adjusting in response to changing operational conditions and application priorities.

### Monitoring and Comparison

The comparison and decision module receives, on one hand, the measured bandwidth values from the monitoring module and, on the other hand, the data transmission requirements of each platform application. The transmission requirements may specify a minimum required data rate, a preferred data rate, latency tolerances, packet loss thresholds, and other parameters relevant to the application's operation.

By comparing each application's requirements against the current capacity of its allocated link, the module continuously evaluates whether each link can adequately support its associated application. This evaluation may take into account not only instantaneous measurements but also predicted changes in link capacity based on the platform's trajectory and known network characteristics.

### Adaptive Response

When the comparison indicates that a link's bandwidth has become insufficient for its application, the information data generator produces information data reflecting the deficiency. This information data is transmitted to the affected application or, alternatively, to a quality of service interface associated with that application.

Upon receiving the information data, the application or its QoS interface adapts its transmission parameters. Such adaptations may include reducing the data transmission rate, changing a compression level, deferring non-critical transmissions, altering the resolution or fidelity of transmitted content, or reprioritizing data streams. In some embodiments, the information data may prompt the application to switch to an alternative communication link with greater available capacity.

### Advantages

By dynamically informing applications of changing link conditions and enabling them to adapt accordingly, the invention ensures that available bandwidth is used efficiently and that transmission attempts remain matched to actual link capacity. This reduces packet loss and retransmission overhead, preserves resources for higher-priority communications, and maintains reliable and stable communication performance despite the continuously varying network conditions inherent to a moving platform.

## Conclusion

The disclosed method and apparatus thus provide an effective solution for managing communications aboard moving platforms. Through continuous bandwidth monitoring, intelligent comparison of application requirements against link capacity, and adaptive prompting of applications and their quality of service interfaces, the system achieves efficient bandwidth utilization and reliable communication under a wide range of operating conditions.

# Patent Abstract

## System and Method for Adaptive Communication Management on a Moving Platform

**ABSTRACT**

A system and method for managing communications on a moving platform hosting a plurality of applications, wherein the system dynamically adapts data transmission based on available communication bandwidth. The system comprises a communication management module operatively coupled to one or more communication links between the moving platform and one or more external networks. The communication management module is configured to monitor available bandwidth across the one or more communication links in real-time and to receive data transmission requests from the plurality of applications executing on the moving platform. A prioritization engine assigns priority levels to the data transmission requests based on predetermined criteria, application type, or quality-of-service requirements. Responsive to detected changes in available bandwidth, the system dynamically allocates bandwidth among the plurality of applications, modifies data compression parameters, adjusts transmission rates, and selectively queues, throttles, or reroutes data transmissions to optimize communication performance. The moving platform may comprise an aircraft, vehicle, vessel, or spacecraft, and the communication links may include satellite, cellular, or terrestrial wireless connections. The system thereby maintains efficient and reliable communications for the plurality of applications despite fluctuating bandwidth conditions encountered during movement of the platform.

---

# Technical Method Summary

## Core Innovation
The invention describes a **communications system for a moving platform** (such as an aircraft, ship, or vehicle) that intelligently manages data distribution across available communication links while enabling applications to adapt to bandwidth constraints.

## Key Technical Components

**1. Multi-Link Data Distribution**
- The system distributes data traffic across multiple supported communication links
- This allows for optimized use of available bandwidth across heterogeneous connection types

**2. Bandwidth Monitoring**
- The system continuously monitors the available bandwidth across the supported links
- It detects conditions where bandwidth becomes **insufficient** to meet current demands

**3. Application Notification Mechanism**
- When bandwidth is inadequate, the system **notifies affected applications**
- This is a proactive feedback loop rather than simply dropping or queuing data

**4. Adaptive Response**
- Upon notification, applications can **adjust their operating parameters**
- This enables graceful degradation—applications reduce their demands to fit available capacity

## Practical Advantage
This method is particularly valuable for **mobile platforms** where connectivity is variable and unpredictable. Rather than experiencing failures when bandwidth drops, the system enables **dynamic adaptation**, allowing applications to maintain functionality at reduced quality/throughput levels.

# PATENT APPLICATION

## APPARATUS AND METHOD FOR OPTIMIZING QUALITY OF SERVICE ON A VEHICLE THROUGH DYNAMIC BANDWIDTH MANAGEMENT

### FIELD OF THE INVENTION

[0001] The present invention relates generally to communication systems for mobile platforms, and more particularly to an apparatus and method for optimizing quality of service (QoS) aboard a vehicle by comparing aggregate bandwidth requirements of a plurality of applications against available communication link capacity and selectively adjusting application data transmission accordingly.

### BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

[0002] Vehicles, including aircraft, watercraft, spacecraft, and terrestrial vehicles, increasingly rely upon wireless communication links to exchange data with external networks and ground-based infrastructure. Such communication links, including satellite links, cellular links, and air-to-ground links, exhibit variable capacity due to factors including atmospheric conditions, geographic position, signal interference, link handoffs, and network congestion.

[0003] Onboard the vehicle, a plurality of applications may concurrently demand access to the communication link, including passenger connectivity services, cockpit or operational data systems, entertainment services, telemetry, and safety-critical communications. When the aggregate bandwidth demanded by these applications exceeds the instantaneously available link capacity, degradation of service, packet loss, and latency may result, adversely affecting higher-priority data flows.

[0004] Accordingly, there exists a need for an apparatus and method that dynamically reconciles application bandwidth requirements with available link capacity to maintain acceptable quality of service across prioritized data flows aboard a vehicle.

### SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0005] In accordance with one embodiment, an apparatus for optimizing quality of service on a vehicle is disclosed, the apparatus comprising: a communication interface configured to communicatively couple the vehicle to at least one communication link; a memory storing bandwidth requirement data associated with a plurality of applications resident on the vehicle; and a processor operatively coupled to the communication interface and the memory.

[0006] The processor is configured to determine an available link capacity of the at least one communication link; determine an aggregate bandwidth requirement of the plurality of applications; compare the aggregate bandwidth requirement against the available link capacity; and, responsive to the comparison indicating that the aggregate bandwidth requirement exceeds the available link capacity, adjust application data associated with at least one of the plurality of applications to conform the aggregate bandwidth requirement to the available link capacity.

[0007] In accordance with another embodiment, a method for optimizing quality of service on a vehicle is disclosed, comprising the steps of monitoring available link capacity, determining bandwidth requirements, comparing said requirements against said capacity, and adjusting application data based upon the comparison.

### BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS

[0008] FIG. 1 is a schematic block diagram of an apparatus for optimizing quality of service aboard a vehicle in accordance with an embodiment of the invention.

[0009] FIG. 2 is a flowchart illustrating a method for optimizing quality of service in accordance with an embodiment of the invention.

[0010] FIG. 3 is a schematic diagram illustrating a prioritization scheme applied to a plurality of applications.

### DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION

[0011] Referring now to FIG. 1, there is depicted an apparatus 100 for optimizing quality of service aboard a vehicle 102. In the illustrated embodiment, the vehicle 102 comprises an aircraft; however, it will be appreciated by those skilled in the art that the vehicle 102 may alternatively comprise a watercraft, spacecraft, rail vehicle, automotive vehicle, or any other mobile platform without departing from the scope of the invention.

[0012] The apparatus 100 includes a communication interface 104 configured to communicatively couple the vehicle 102 to one or more communication links 106. The one or more communication links 106 may include, without limitation, a satellite communication link, an air-to-ground link, a cellular link, a line-of-sight radio frequency link, or any combination thereof. The communication interface 104 may include one or more transceivers, antennas, modems, and associated circuitry.

[0013] The apparatus 100 further includes a processor 108 operatively coupled to a memory 110. The processor 108 may comprise one or more general-purpose processors, digital signal processors, application-specific integrated circuits, field-programmable gate arrays, or any combination thereof. The memory 110 may comprise any suitable non-transitory computer-readable storage medium and stores instructions executable by the processor 108, as well as bandwidth requirement data 112 associated with a plurality of applications 114a-114n resident on or in communication with the vehicle 102.

[0014] The plurality of applications 114a-114n may include, by way of example and not limitation, passenger internet connectivity applications, in-flight entertainment applications, operational and avionics data applications, crew communication applications, telemetry applications, and safety-critical messaging applications. Each application may be associated with a respective priority level and a respective bandwidth requirement.

[0015] In operation, the processor 108 is configured to determine an available link capacity of the one or more communication links 106. The available link capacity may be determined by any suitable means, including measuring a data throughput of the communication interface 104, receiving link capacity information from a network element, monitoring signal quality metrics such as signal-to-noise ratio or bit error rate, or estimating capacity based upon geographic position and a lookup table of expected capacities.

[0016] The processor 108 is further configured to determine an aggregate bandwidth requirement of the plurality of applications 114a-114n. In one embodiment, the aggregate bandwidth requirement is determined by summing individual bandwidth requirements retrieved from the bandwidth requirement data 112. In an alternative embodiment, the individual bandwidth requirements are dynamically measured based upon actual or requested data flows associated with each application.

[0017] The processor 108 compares the aggregate bandwidth requirement against the available link capacity. Responsive to the comparison indicating that the aggregate bandwidth requirement exceeds the available link capacity, the processor 108 adjusts application data associated with at least one of the plurality of applications 114a-114n so as to conform the aggregate bandwidth requirement to the available link capacity.

[0018] In accordance with one embodiment, adjusting the application data comprises one or more of: throttling a data rate associated with at least one application; compressing data associated with at least one application; buffering or delaying transmission of data associated with at least one application; transcoding media data to a lower bitrate; suspending transmission of data associated with at least one application; and reallocating bandwidth among applications in accordance with the respective priority levels.

[0019] Referring now to FIG. 3, in a preferred embodiment, the plurality of applications 114a-114n are assigned to a hierarchy of priority levels. When the aggregate bandwidth requirement exceeds the available link capacity, the processor 108 preferentially reduces bandwidth allocated to applications of lower priority before reducing bandwidth allocated to applications of higher priority. In this manner, safety-critical and operational data flows are preserved while discretionary data flows, such as passenger entertainment, are adjusted to accommodate the available link capacity.

[0020] In a further embodiment, the processor 108 is configured to repeat the foregoing determination, comparison, and adjustment steps on a periodic or event-driven basis, thereby dynamically adapting to changes in available link capacity and changes in application bandwidth demand. An event triggering re-evaluation may include, without limitation, a change in link capacity exceeding a threshold, a handoff between communication links, the initiation or termination of an application, or expiration of a timing interval.

[0021] Referring now to FIG. 2, a method 200 for optimizing quality of service aboard a vehicle is illustrated. At step 202, the available link capacity of at least one communication link is determined. At step 204, an aggregate bandwidth requirement of a plurality of applications is determined. At step 206, the aggregate bandwidth requirement is compared against the available link capacity.

[0022] At decision step 208, if the aggregate bandwidth requirement does not exceed the available link capacity, the method returns to step 202. If the aggregate bandwidth requirement exceeds the available link capacity, the method proceeds to step 210, wherein application data associated with at least one of the plurality of applications is adjusted in accordance with a prioritization scheme so as to conform the aggregate bandwidth requirement to the available link capacity. The method thereafter returns to step 202 for continued monitoring.

[0023] In a further embodiment, the method further comprises the step of allocating, when the available link capacity exceeds the aggregate bandwidth requirement, surplus link capacity to one or more applications to enhance quality of service, such as by increasing a permitted data rate or media quality of one or more applications.

[0024] While the invention has been described with reference to certain embodiments, it will be understood by those skilled in the art that various changes may be made and equivalents may be substituted without departing from the scope of the invention. Therefore, it is intended that the invention not be limited to the particular embodiments disclosed, but that the invention will include all embodiments falling within the scope of the appended claims.

### CLAIMS

What is claimed is:

1. An apparatus for optimizing quality of service on a vehicle, comprising:
   a communication interface configured to communicatively couple the vehicle to at least one communication link;
   a memory storing bandwidth requirement data associated with a plurality of applications resident on the vehicle; and
   a processor operatively coupled to the communication interface and the memory, the processor configured to:
   determine an available link capacity of the at least one communication link;
   determine an aggregate bandwidth requirement of the plurality of applications;
   compare the aggregate bandwidth requirement against the available link capacity; and
   responsive to the aggregate bandwidth requirement exceeding the available link capacity, adjust application data associated with at least one of the plurality of applications to conform the aggregate bandwidth requirement to the available link capacity.

2. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the vehicle comprises an aircraft, and the at least one communication link comprises at least one of a satellite communication link and an air-to-ground communication link.

3. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein each of the plurality of applications is associated with a respective priority level, and wherein the processor is configured to adjust the application data in accordance with the respective priority levels.

4. The apparatus of claim 3, wherein the processor is configured to preferentially reduce bandwidth allocated to an application of a lower priority level before reducing bandwidth allocated to an application of a higher priority level.

5. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein adjusting the application data comprises at least one of throttling a data rate, compressing data, buffering data, transcoding media data to a lower bitrate, and suspending transmission of data.

6. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the processor is configured to determine the available link capacity based upon at least one of a measured data throughput, a signal quality metric, and a geographic position of the vehicle.

7. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the processor is further configured to allocate surplus link capacity to at least one application when the available link capacity exceeds the aggregate bandwidth requirement.

8. A method for optimizing quality of service on a vehicle, comprising:
